newsitem.title: UK: LME aluminium eyes upside in inter-office trade.
newsitem.headline: LME aluminium eyes upside in inter-office trade.

text.p: London Metal Exchange (LME) aluminium prices were steadier above the $1,600 level during inter-office trade on Monday, while the other base metals slumbered.
Aluminium initially rose in Asian trading, then extended gains on forward buying in early Europe, traders said.
Three months aluminium was last quoted at $1,610/12 per tonne, compared to Friday's kerb close of $1,597.
"It went up to around $1,603 overnight because of the weaker dollar/yen, but it got sold down again first thing this morning on profit-taking," a trader said.
But aluminium prices then started ticking higher again on forward buying at the start of European trading, with good volumes seen in the $1,603-$1,613 area.
An LME stock drawdown of 3,400 tonnes was also supportive.
"LME stocks fell by 16,050 tonnes during (last) week and it is difficult to get too bearish about the market in the face of this steady stock drawdown," brokers Brandeis said in a report.
Tough resistance in the $1,610-$1,620 price band needed to be overcome for further upside progress, traders said.
Copper, by contrast, was dull and indicated just $2 firmer at $2,489. Cash to threes backwardation was slightly wider at $65/$68, versus $59/$64 on Friday.
"Copper is just dead this morning," a trader said.
Analysts said copper's technicals and fundamentals were more or less neutral and needed some outside impetus to force prices out of the recent $2,460-$2,500 price range
The other base metals were also little changed from Friday's closing levels.
Zinc was steady after seeing good two-way business at the $1,370 level and was holding at $1,367/$1,370, versus $1,367.
Lead was quiet at $642/$645, compared to $642 ,and nickel was also virtually unchanged at $7,310/20.
Tin at $5,680/700, was off slighlty from its previous $5,710 close, but traders said it would look to build a base after making strong gains on Friday. The next upside level was $5,800.
Alloy was quiet and indicated at $1,480/90, versus $1,470/75.
